name: Nirvana
reference: Smells Like Teen Spirit / Breed / In Bloom — Nevermind (1991), prod. Butch Vig, mixed by Andy Wallace, Sound City
rig: Kurt Cobain: '69 Fender Competition Mustang / '65 Jaguar (DiMarzio Super Distortion) -> Boss DS-1 (tone ~10 o'clock, level max) [+ ProCo RAT, EHX Small Clone] -> Mesa/Boogie Studio Preamp -> Crown Power Base 2 -> 4x12, double-tracked with a Fender Bassman on the heavy parts (AC30 for cleans); SM57/U87/414 close, very little room
notes: Dual-rig stereo for Vig's double-tracked rhythms: DS-1 (always on) feeds both; left = Mesa Studio Preamp (preamp-only capture, the Crown SS power amp assumed clean) + Nevermind-matched T75 4x12 IR, right = '71 Bassman DI at a pedal-platform setting + a second Nevermind IR, hard-panned. Exact Bassman year and Kurt's preamp settings are unknown (guesses). Small Clone can't be modelled: SW7 (spread) is preset with wobble as a stand-in for the watery verse/Come As You Are chorus. No reverb: Vig kept the guitars dry and in your face. Echo is only a solo helper (not on the record). SW8 = RAT stacked for extra saturation.

left.label: ProCo RAT 2 low (D3 F5 L6), stacks on DS-1
Boss DS-1, tone 4 dist 7 (Kurt's Nevermind DS-1)
Mesa/Boogie Studio Preamp rhythm ch, heavy edge V9 bright off (preamp only)

right.label: 1971 Fender Bassman normal ch, sweet spot V7 T8 B5
